The orchestrator reconciles each token against on-disk `.faff/runs/<run-id>/ISSUE-XX/` artifacts + git ground truth (never the subagent transcript) before recording the ledger bucket. **Turn-survival invariant.** **Every** Agent-tool dispatch this orchestrator makes — a build, a prep producer, any producer, and whatever transport other prose here names — must hold a **turn-safe posture**: foreground (**`run_in_background: false`**) when its result is consumed inline, covered by an executor's await-all gate, or harness-tracked-background under a harness that re-invokes the parent on child completion (gateway → **Producer dispatch**); where the stranding premise holds — the autonomous orchestrator runs headless / with a live run dir, so it always does — the orchestrator must **never end a turn with a dispatched agent still in flight**, because an idle unattended parent is reaped and takes the in-flight agent down with it (gateway → **Producer dispatch** for the background-by-default *why*). This binds even the prep-via-Agent-tool path below, without rewriting that transport prose. The **`faff inflightcheck`** Stop hook is this posture's mechanical backstop on the Agent-dispatch arm: a per-dispatch **in-flight marker** written before each Agent dispatch and cleared on its return, so a turn that nonetheless ends with a dispatch still outstanding is refused at turn-end where the stranding premise holds (the autonomous orchestrator runs headless / with a live run dir, so it always does; a harness that re-invokes the parent gets a non-blocking note instead) — the arm `background-fence` abstains from. But `inflightcheck` is **enumeration-based** — it refuses turn-end only for a per-dispatch marker that was explicitly opened, so a dispatch shape nobody bracketed (a subprocess `spawn`, a retry) can still strand the run. The **`faff turncheck`** Stop hook is the **state-based** complement: it reads `owner.status` itself and refuses a **non-terminal turn-end** — a turn ending while the run is still `owner.status:"running"` with a clean queue and nothing legitimately in flight — so a strand is caught regardless of which dispatch type left it. The three compose disjointly, one hook per case: `runcheck` owns an undispatched queue, `inflightcheck` an open marker, `turncheck` the running-but-clean-and-quiet residual. Its detective half is `faff disposition`, which now flags the same bare `owner.status:"running"` state post-mortem (the mid-prep-death blind spot). *Prep-producer isolation is a deferred sibling (the inline prep producer is the same bloat class but its subagent dispatch was scoped out of the build-isolation work); the floor covers builds only until that lands, at which point the prep producer is folded into the same wording.*

## Park protocol and tracker tagging

Beep-boop itself rarely parks — its sub-skills do (build-queue assembly's own `needs-decision-first` resolve-attempt, above, is the exception: beep-boop runs that Park-protocol invocation itself). But whenever a sub-skill, or beep-boop's own step-4 resolve-attempt, returns `parked` for an issue, beep-boop's park backstop confirms:

1. The tracker comment written by the sub-skill (or beep-boop itself) is present on the issue.
2. The issue carries the `faff-parked` tag (or tracker-equivalent label). If the sub-skill didn't apply it, beep-boop does — via `faff label add <issue> faff-parked` and its descriptor's write (gateway → **Control-label provisioning**).
3. The per-issue log directory (`.faff/runs/<run-id>/ISSUE-XX/`) has the `parked` reason written to a top-level `park.md`, and the park's fact — `{ issue_id, root_cause_class, timestamp }` — is recorded in the run's shared `park_records` accumulator (gateway → **Park protocol (shared)** → _the accumulator and render boundary_), which beep-boop **owns** for the whole run: it receives park facts from sub-skill returns and from this backstop alike, deduplicates a retry or a rediscovery of the same completed transition, and renders the accumulator exactly once at run end, in the summary's canonical `faff-parks` fence (see _Reporting_ below).

This is what `/faff-wtf` looks for to surface parked issues in the morning, and what `faff park-history` reads to detect a repeat-parked issue.

## Reporting

All human-facing output beep-boop emits — its run summary, the run-summary tracker status post, park comments, and discovered-scope tickets it files — passes through the configured `rendering_adaptor` normalise pass **before it is printed or written** (gateway → **Rendering**, Universal-routing rule), so enumerable sets render as lists, never `·`/comma run-on paragraphs (the prose-skimmability rule). The table-vs-definition-list rule is part of that pass.

On run completion, after `faff run close` (it appends the `run-end` event and pumps andon; a fail-closed `run open` did both itself), produce:

### 1. `.faff/runs/<run-id>/summary.md`

Write the facts file, then render the summary with one call. It writes `summary.md` and prints the same bytes:

```bash
"$faff" run summary --run-dir "$FAFF_RUN_DIR" --facts "$FAFF_RUN_DIR/summary-facts.json"
```

The command computes everything faff can read itself: the outcome buckets and annotation arrays, the header, unit economics, install health, PR numbers, superseded ids, the holdout split and the ground-truth divergences. A missing or malformed facts file renders a `⚠ could not read facts` line at exit 0; exit 2 means the ledger itself is unreadable. Lines built from the facts file end ` _(reported)_`.
